newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BBA to look for new banking opportunities.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BBA to look for new banking opportunities.

text.p: Brazil's Banco BBA Creditanstalt will be looking for new opportunities in the banking sector after a deal with local bank BCN failed to develop, BBA president Fernao Bracher said.

"The acquisition and co-operation with BCN were part of our strategy, but the deal was not possible. Now this is time for reflection and we will be looking into all possibilities," Bracher told Reuters.
In a statement published Thursday, BCN said it ended talks with Banco BBA and has decided not to sell a controlling stake to the bank.
Instead of selling control of the bank to BBA, BCN said it would soon announce a new management model under which the bank would be administered by a "shareholder company, made up of BCN executives."
The statement also said the new management model should be in place in a maximum period of six months.
Bracher said Banco BBA could reconsider the privatization of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj, which has been postponed twice already and is now expected for February.
Banco BBA had pre-qualified for the auction but dropped out of the running to purchase the acquisition of the BCN stake to expand its retail activities.
Bracher said he was disappointed and surprised at the outcome of the negotiations. He said that continuing speculation over the deal might have weighed on BCN president Pedro Conde's decision.
The latest speculation in the press was that Banco BBA already had been laying off BCN executives.
Banco BBA Creditanstalt is a wholesale bank, whose main shareholders are Fernao Bracher, Antonio Beltran Martinez and Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein, which owns 49 percent of the bank's capital.
